evidence_quotes: 45 recorded events occurred over the 31-day window
Magnitudes ranged from M4.0 to M5.7, with an average of M4.63
Three separate events reached the M5.7 peak: Tobelo, Indonesia (Feb 14); San Alejandro, Peru (Feb 5); and Mariana Islands region (Jan 28)
Tobelo, Indonesia was the clear hotspot, accounting for 8 of the 45 events (18%)
a M5.7 strike near the Kermadec Islands on February 8, at only 5.7 km depth
the Mariana Islands region (4 events, including a M5.4)
criticisms: The report states 'Three separate events reached the M5.7 peak: Tobelo, Indonesia (Feb 14); San Alejandro, Peru (Feb 5); and Mariana Islands region (Jan 28).' The Jan 28 event in the digest is listed as '104 km E of Mariana Islands region' at M5.7 — this is technically correct but the report simplifies it to 'Mariana Islands region', which is a minor imprecision rather than a fabrication.
The report describes the period as '31-day window' — Jan 17 to Feb 16 is actually 30 days inclusive, a minor arithmetic imprecision.
The report says 'the busiest single day being February 3 (4 events)' — this is confirmed by the daily_counts showing 2026-02-03: 4, which is the highest single-day count. This is correct.

The Mariana Islands region M5.4 event cited is traceable to the Jan 30 sample event ('86 km E of Mariana Islands region', M5.4), which is accurate but the report attributes it to the Mariana Islands region cluster of 4 events — this is consistent with the top_regions data.
No invented locations, magnitudes, depths, or tsunami flags were detected. All claims are traceable to the digest.
